## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12668#issuecomment-5790106868) and the [author reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12668#issuecomment-5790136357), checked at `57eae287a682dc35d3fad0eca19ef34d9906ec99`.

**Verified:** The nested symlink loop finding is resolved. `find -H` follows only the command-line roots, so interior loops are no longer traversed, and symlinked roots still contribute files. The reply's description of `-H` matches findutils source and the synthetic runs. No regression was found in the new commit.

### Nested symlink loops: resolved

Same synthetic tree as before (`Pictures/sub/loop -> Pictures/`), selector stub returning `x.jpg`:

| Revision | `find` mode | Selection returned | `omarchy-menu-file` exit | `omarchy-transcode` (stubbed) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Base | plain | `x.jpg` | 0 | continues to format menu |
| Earlier head `548effc` | `-L` | `x.jpg` | 1 | aborts after the pick |
| Current head `57eae28` | `-H` | `x.jpg` | 0 | continues to format menu |

**Verified:** A symlinked root, a symlinked root containing interior loops, and three mixed roots (absolute symlink, real directory, relative symlink) all return the expected files at the current head. Interior symlinks now behave as they did at base: they are no longer followed, as the new code comment states.

### #12665 argument-size limit: still present, and the PR still closes the issue

The selector is unchanged and still passes the whole option list as one argument, as noted in the earlier review. In a synthetic run, 1541 options with paths averaging 91 bytes failed with `Argument list too long` (exit 126) at both base and head; 800 options succeeded. The reporter's library was not reproduced.

**Impact:** The reply says the size limit is not claimed fixed, but the PR body still says `Closes #12665`, and GitHub lists #12665 as a closing reference. Merging would close the issue while the large-library failure it also reports remains.

**Suggested change:** Replace `Closes #12665` with a non-closing reference (for example `Part of #12665`), or open a separate issue for the argument-size limit. The PR description's "Pass `-L` to `find`" also no longer matches the code.

**Optional (pre-existing error handling):** `pipefail` still turns any nonzero `find` exit into failure after a successful pick, not only loop errors. An unreadable subdirectory is one example. This behaviour exists at base, but this PR now traverses symlinked roots, so it can occur on the newly fixed path. For example, a root linked to a mount point with an unreadable `lost+found`: in synthetic runs with a mode-000 directory, the pick was returned, then the script exited 1. `omarchy-transcode` aborts in that case, and `omarchy-games-retro-install` treats it as a cancel. One option is `{ find -H "${find_args[@]}" 2>/dev/null || true; } | sort -rn | ...`. An empty list still makes the selector exit 1. Whether this belongs in this PR is a scope decision.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `57eae287a682dc35d3fad0eca19ef34d9906ec99`, compared with base and the earlier head. Isolated synthetic directory trees with the real `omarchy-menu-file`, `omarchy-transcode` and `omarchy-games-retro-install` scripts, stubbed selector UI and shell, plus source inspection of these scripts and GNU findutils 4.11.0. No real menu UI, transcoding, RetroArch, user media or ext4 `lost+found` was tested. The unreadable-directory cases used synthetic mode-000 directories.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh (source plus synthetic runs) and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh (source and GitHub metadata) technical assessments, with one targeted follow-up to the Sol assessment. Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
